Country B has the comparative advantage in corn, and Country A has the comparative advantage in soybeans. is incorrect: Reverses the opportunity-cost comparison.
Country B has the comparative advantage in both goods because it has the higher output of soybeans. is incorrect: Uses one output number to claim an advantage in both goods.

payload.stem: A central bank carries out expansionary monetary policy in an economy with ample reserves, and the exchange rate floats. Which of the following correctly describes the chain of effects in the short run?

options.text: Interest rates fall, net financial capital outflows rise, the currency depreciates, net exports rise, and aggregate demand shifts left, offsetting the policy.
options.why: Gets the final AD shift backward; net exports are a component of AD and reinforce the policy.

options.text: Interest rates fall, net financial capital outflows rise, the currency depreciates, net exports rise, and aggregate demand shifts right further.
options.why: Policy changes interest rates, which change capital flows and the exchange rate, which change net exports and reinforce the shift in AD.

options.text: Interest rates fall, net financial capital outflows rise, the currency depreciates, net exports fall, and aggregate demand shifts left further.

options.why: Starts from the wrong interest-rate effect of the policy.

options.text: Interest rates fall and nothing else changes, because the exchange rate is not affected by interest rates.
options.why: Ignores that interest rates change capital flows and the exchange rate.
